Rauwend is the gray, windswept face of Azzagrat where sound, sensation, direction, and recollection are subdued. Vaelzhar is a colossal draconic planar nail binding that law to the Abyssal twin of Palanthas. Its presence makes records fade, streets become difficult to remember, and witnesses forget the sequence of events they just survived.

Abyssal Origin: Layer 46 of Azzagrat — Shadowsky
Palanthas Anchor: the Tower of High Sorcery, Shoikan Grove, and the city's magical geometry.

Shadowsky is illuminated from below and throws darkness upward into the heavens. Nythravel embodies that inversion. Its own shadow rises independently of its flesh, and in its wake doors, towers, and roads cease to agree on direction.

Kharzoryx, the Blue Pyre

Species: Voorz’zt Coldfire Wyrm
Abyssal Origin: Layer 47 of Azzagrat — Voorz’zt
Palanthas Anchor: the northern approaches and the city's physical laws of heat, cold, destruction, and defence.

Voorz’zt lies beneath a wan blue sun where thermal laws contradict themselves. Kharzoryx breathes blue fire that freezes and commands frost that burns. Its approach causes hearths to rim with ice and snow to scorch skin.
biography.public: A colossal demonic wyrm wreathed in blue flame whose heat freezes and whose frost burns.

biography.value: The first things through the Portal. They obey, and they count the days.

description.value: While the binding holds, the creature cannot attack, harm, or knowingly permit harm to come to the wizard whose seal it bears. It will obey the letter of an instruction and nothing more.
Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.
The demon makes two claw attacks.

biography.value: The commonest thing Raistlin pulls through the Portal. It answers to a true name, it does what it is told, and it counts.

dr.custom: bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks

description.value: While bound by a true name, the tormentor cannot willingly disobey a direct instruction from its binder, and cannot attack the binder. It obeys the letter of every instruction and never the intent.
The tormentor has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.
The tormentor knows exactly how many days it has been bound, who bound it, and every instruction it has been given. If ever released, it acts on all of this.
The tormentor makes two claw attacks and one bite.
Plus 7 (2d6) necrotic damage.

biography.value: What the Black Host actually looks like on a battlefield. Dragonarmy formations break rather than receive a charge from these.

description.value: If the warbeast moves at least 20 feet straight toward a target and hits it with a gore attack on the same turn, the target takes an extra 10 (3d6) piercing damage and must succeed on a DC 16 Strength saving throw or be knocked prone.
The warbeast deals double damage to objects and structures.
The warbeast makes one gore attack and two claw attacks.

biography.value: What Raistlin sends at fortifications. It was doing this work long before anyone summoned it and shows every sign of having missed it.

description.value: The siegebreaker deals double damage to objects and structures.
Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.
While bound, it cannot attack its binder or disobey a direct instruction. It will interpret 'clear the wall' as broadly as the wording allows.
The siegebreaker makes two slam attacks.
The target must succeed on a DC 18 Strength saving throw or be knocked prone.

biography.value: From the Field of Lost Names. It has forgotten its own name and wants yours — not to use, simply to have.

description.value: Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.
The demon cannot be targeted by any effect that requires knowing a creature's name, including binding rituals and the Bell of True Names. It is aware of this and it is why it is still free.
The demon makes three claw attacks, or two and uses Take the Name.

One creature within 30 feet must succeed on a DC 17 Charisma saving throw or forget its own name for 1 hour. While it does, it cannot be the target of any spell that names it, cannot be raised from the dead, and has disadvantage on Charisma checks. A greater restoration or the Bell of True Names ends this early.
When a creature attempts to bind the demon, it may force the caster to make a DC 17 Charisma saving throw. On a failure, the binding fails and the caster takes 22 (5d8) psychic damage.

actors.name: Warden of the Palace of Chains

biography.value: Keeper of the mechanism through which dominion resurrection functions. It did not build the Palace. It maintains it, meticulously, and can explain exactly what the party will break.

description.value: If the Warden fails a saving throw, it can choose to succeed instead.
The Warden knows the true name of every soul bound in the Palace, including any the party is trying to free. It will trade one, honestly, for something it wants.
Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.
The Warden makes two chain attacks and uses Bind.
The target is grappled (escape DC 19) if it is Large or smaller.

One creature the Warden can see within 60 feet must succeed on a DC 19 Charisma saving throw or be restrained by spectral chains for 1 minute. While restrained this way, the creature cannot take reactions and its speed is 0. It repeats the save at the end of each of its turns.
Each creature restrained by the Warden takes 10 (3d6) force damage.
The Warden speaks one true name. That creature has disadvantage on saving throws against the Warden until the end of its next turn.
The Warden teleports up to 60 feet and makes one chain attack.

prototypeToken.name: Warden of the Palace of Chains

biography.value: Takhisis does not come herself until the end. She sends this, and it speaks with her voice, and it is authorised to offer terms.

dr.custom: bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks

description.value: If the Herald fails a saving throw, it can choose to succeed instead.
Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.
The Herald can speak as Takhisis. Once per encounter it may make an offer to a named creature; the offer is genuine and will be honoured, and the DM should make it genuinely tempting.
The Herald cannot be surprised, has advantage on saves against being blinded, deafened, stunned or knocked unconscious, and can take one extra reaction per round.
The Herald makes one bite and two claw attacks, or uses Chromatic Breath.

Recharge 5–6. The Herald exhales in a 90-foot cone. Choose acid, cold, fire, lightning or poison. Each creature makes a DC 22 Dexterity saving throw, taking 66 (12d10) damage of the chosen type on a failure, or half on a success.
The Herald makes a Wisdom (Perception) check.
The Herald makes one claw attack.
One creature the Herald can see within 60 feet must succeed on a DC 22 Wisdom saving throw or use its reaction to move up to its speed and make one weapon attack against a target the Herald chooses.

biography.value: Desperate rather than wicked. Refugees have made a great many of these this season.
Conscripted, badly trained, and more frightened of their officers than of the party.

description.value: The recruit has advantage on an attack roll against a creature if at least one of its allies is within 5 feet of the creature and the ally is not incapacitated.

biography.value: Not a Knight. A levy from Solanthus or Kalaman with three weeks of drill and a spear, standing where they were told to stand.

description.value: The soldier has advantage on attack rolls against a creature if at least one other Solamnic soldier is within 5 feet of it and not incapacitated.

biography.value: Astinus's order of scholars. They do not intervene in history. They record it, and several of them find this harder than they will admit.

description.value: The Aesthetic can recall any passage it has read. It has advantage on Intelligence (History) checks and automatically succeeds on any check to remember something recorded in the Great Library.
The Aesthetic will not take a hostile action, even in self-defence, unless the Library itself is threatened. It will help the wounded, and considers that a different category.

biography.value: Palanthas has not been attacked in living memory and its guard reflects that. Polite, well-equipped, and entirely unprepared for what is coming.

description.value: Within Palanthas, the guard can call for reinforcements as an action. 1d4 more guards arrive in 1d6 rounds.

biography.value: The reason the Tower holds as long as it does. Knows the walls better than the Knights commanding them and says so.

description.value: Over 10 minutes the engineer can reinforce a 20-foot section of wall or a gate, granting it +5 AC and 50 temporary hit points until the end of the siege.
While directing a siege weapon, the engineer's attacks with it gain a +4 bonus to hit and deal an additional 10 (3d6) damage.

biography.value: Dracart's former apprentice. He has run for four months and he is nearly finished.

description.value: The draconian corruption ritual is scarified into Krell's body in eleven incomplete overlapping passes. It cannot be copied, transcribed, imaged or scried. Destroying the knowledge means killing him.
Krell has three levels of exhaustion and cannot remove them while pursued. He will not mention this.

Krell is a 5th-level spellcaster. Spell save DC 13, +5 to hit. Cantrips: Mage Hand, Minor Illusion, Prestidigitation, Grave Whisper. 1st (4 slots): Shield, Disguise Self, Comprehend Languages. 2nd (3): Invisibility, Misty Step. 3rd (2): Nondetection. Order spells (Black Robes): Blood Scent, Feign Life. Exhaustion and four months of running have left him with nothing offensive prepared, and he will spend every slot on getting away.

Scribed and owned, and not among today's preparations; any of these can be prepared after a long rest. Spellbook (unprepared): Alarm, Detect Magic, Identify, Feather Fall, Find Familiar, Floating Disk.

biography.value: Career soldiers who have taken cities and expect to take more.

description.value: The veteran has advantage on saving throws against being frightened while it can see an allied officer within 30 feet.
The veteran makes two longsword attacks.

biography.value: The first Order of the Knighthood: loyalty and obedience. Crowns are the youngest Knights and the ones most likely to die proving something.

description.value: The Knight has advantage on saving throws against being frightened or charmed while an ally it has sworn to protect is within 30 feet.
When reduced to 0 hit points but not killed outright, the Knight may choose to drop to 1 hit point instead. Once per long rest, and only while defending a position it has been ordered to hold.
The Knight makes two longsword attacks.

biography.value: Runs the gate the party has to get through. Not corrupt, not stupid, and extremely tired of people with sealed letters from wizards.

description.value: The captain has advantage on Wisdom (Insight) checks made to determine whether someone is lying about their business in the city.
The captain makes two longsword attacks.

biography.value: Commander Veyrath's people. They are not trying to capture the party. They are trying to find out where the party is going.

description.value: The agent has advantage on Wisdom (Insight) checks made to determine whether a creature is lying, and on Charisma (Deception) checks made to maintain a cover identity it has held for at least a day.
When subjected to an effect allowing a Dexterity save for half damage, the agent takes no damage on a success and half on a failure.
The agent makes two rapier attacks.
When a creature the agent can see ends its turn within 30 feet, the agent moves up to its speed without provoking opportunity attacks and attempts to hide.

biography.value: Wizards from various centuries who came for the Tower and were neither admitted nor released. They are helpful, at length, and accurate as of whichever decade they entered.

description.value: The wanderer's knowledge is accurate for the century in which it entered the forest. Several do not know the Kingpriest is dead. None of them can be convinced of the current date.
The wanderer cannot be removed from the Forest of Wayreth by any means, including plane shift and wish. Attempts simply return it to where it was.

biography.value: They earned the rank and intend to keep it. Killing the officer is usually worth more than killing four soldiers.

description.value: Allied Dragonarmy creatures within 30 feet that can hear the officer have advantage on saving throws against being charmed or frightened.
When the officer scores a critical hit with a melee weapon, it rolls one additional damage die.
The officer makes three attacks with its glaive.
The officer adds 3 to its AC against one melee attack that would hit it. To do so, it must see the attacker and be wielding a melee weapon.

biography.value: The second Order: courage and faith. Swords carry the Knighthood's religious authority, which after the Cataclysm was an awkward thing to carry and is suddenly not.

description.value: The Knight is a 5th-level spellcaster. Spell save DC 14, +6 to hit. Cantrips: Guidance, Sacred Flame, Thaumaturgy, Resistance. 1st (4 slots): Bless, Cure Wounds, Shield of Faith, Sanctuary. 2nd (3): Aid, Lesser Restoration. 3rd (2): Beacon of Hope, Dispel Magic.
The Knight has advantage on saving throws against being frightened, and cannot be forced to move against its will while it holds ground it has been ordered to defend.
The Knight makes two longsword attacks and one shield bash.
Plus 7 (2d6) radiant damage against fiends and undead.
When a creature the Knight can see within 5 feet is hit by an attack, the Knight may take the hit instead.

biography.value: Renegades, mostly. The Conclave keeps a list and the list gets longer every season.

description.value: 9th-level spellcaster. Spell save DC 15, +7 to hit. Cantrips: Fire Bolt, Mage Hand, Minor Illusion, Prestidigitation. 1st (4 slots): Mage Armor, Magic Missile, Shield. 2nd (3): Misty Step, Scorching Ray. 3rd (3): Counterspell, Fireball, Fly, Dispel Magic. 4th (3): Greater Invisibility, Wall of Fire, Dimension Door. 5th (1): Cone of Cold.

Scribed and owned, and not among today's preparations; any of these can be prepared after a long rest. Spellbook (unprepared): Burning Hands, Feather Fall, Detect Magic, Web, Haste, Lightning Bolt, Hypnotic Pattern, Animate Objects, Scrying.
The battle mage has never taken the Test of High Sorcery and cannot Overreach. It has disadvantage on saving throws against spells cast by a Wizard of High Sorcery who names it renegade aloud.

biography.value: Senior Dragonarmy intelligence. He will buy the party dinner, be honest about who he is, ask good questions, and leave the conversation ahead. Fighting him means you have lost the character.

description.value: Veyrath knows when a creature is lying to him unless it succeeds on a DC 18 Charisma (Deception) check. He rarely lets on.
Veyrath does not attempt to capture or kill the party while he believes following them is more informative. He is usually correct about that.
Veyrath makes three rapier attacks.
When reduced below half hit points, Veyrath may disengage, move up to his speed, and issue an order allowing one ally to do the same.

biography.value: A dark elf of Silvanesti, exiled for worshipping Nuitari, newly apprenticed at Wayreth. He is spying on Raistlin for the Conclave. Raistlin knows and permitted it.

description.value: Dalamar has advantage on saving throws against effects that would compel him to reveal information, and on Deception checks made to conceal his loyalties. He is not certain himself which way he would jump.

12th-level wizard. Spell save DC 16, +8 to hit. Cantrips: Grave Whisper, Cinder Lash, Mage Hand, Minor Illusion, Prestidigitation. 1st (4 slots): Charm Person, Shield, Mage Armor. 2nd (3): Invisibility, Misty Step. 3rd (3): Counterspell, Fear, Dispel Magic. 4th (3): Greater Invisibility, Dimension Door. 5th (2): Dominate Person. 6th (1): Disintegrate. Order spells (Black Robes): Umbral Burst, Sable Edict, Tyrant's Brand, Death's Due.

Scribed and owned, and not among today's preparations; any of these can be prepared after a long rest. Spellbook (unprepared): Comprehend Languages, Detect Magic, Identify, Blackflame Dart, Obedient Step, Blood Scent, Feign Life, Bestow Curse, Animate Dead, Life Transfer, Transfer Essence, Crown of Submission.

biography.value: A renegade Black Robe in Dragonarmy service who wants Ossian Krell dead rather than recovered, and is exceeding her orders. She will explain her reasoning and the party may well agree with it.

description.value: Mereth's position is that the corruption ritual should not exist, that the Conclave will not destroy it, and that she is therefore going to. Play her as correct and let the party argue.

10th-level spellcaster. Spell save DC 16, +8 to hit. Cantrips: Fire Bolt, Mage Hand, Minor Illusion, Grave Whisper, Nuitari's Hook. 1st (4 slots): Shield, Mage Armor, Magic Missile. 2nd (3): Misty Step. 3rd (3): Counterspell, Fireball, Dispel Magic. 4th (3): Greater Invisibility, Blight. 5th (2): Cone of Cold. Order spells (Black Robes): Blackflame Dart, Blood Scent, Harvest the Fallen, Starless Lance. Losing the Conclave's sanction cost her its protection, not the magic she had already learned.

Scribed and owned, and not among today's preparations; any of these can be prepared after a long rest. Spellbook (unprepared): Detect Magic, Disguise Self, Borrowed Vitality, Obedient Step, Feign Life, Umbral Burst, Sable Edict, Dimension Door, Life Transfer, Curse the Magi.

biography.value: The best recurring antagonist in the campaign precisely because they are right. They will negotiate, and they will stop if the target agrees to take the Test.

description.value: Advantage on attack rolls and saving throws against any creature it has formally declared renegade. It always declares first; it considers this a matter of professional pride.
The hunter may cast counterspell twice per long rest without expending a slot.

9th-level spellcaster. Spell save DC 15, +7 to hit. Cantrips: Mage Hand, Minor Illusion, Ray of Frost, Message. 1st (4 slots): Shield, Detect Magic, Magic Missile. 2nd (3): Misty Step, Hold Person, Detect Thoughts, See Invisibility. 3rd (3): Counterspell, Hypnotic Pattern, Dispel Magic. 4th (3): Dimension Door. 5th (1): Hold Monster.

Scribed and owned, and not among today's preparations; any of these can be prepared after a long rest. Spellbook (unprepared): Alarm, Comprehend Languages, Identify, Protection from Evil and Good, Locate Object, Nondetection, Clairvoyance, Fly, Arcane Eye, Scrying.
The hunter makes two shortsword attacks.

One creature within 60 feet must succeed on a DC 16 Charisma saving throw. On a failure, for 1 minute, whenever it casts a spell it must first succeed on a DC 16 Constitution saving throw or the spell fails and the slot is expended. 3/day.

biography.value: The third Order: wisdom and justice. A Rose commands, and the whole apparatus of the Knighthood is arranged so that the Rose is the one who has to decide.

description.value: Allies within 30 feet that can see and hear the Knight add +2 to saving throws and cannot be frightened.
The Knight and allies within 10 feet are immune to the frightened condition.

The Knight is a 9th-level spellcaster. Spell save DC 16, +8 to hit. 1st (4 slots): Bless, Heroism, Command, Cure Wounds, Shield of Faith. 2nd (3): Aid, Warding Bond, Lesser Restoration. 3rd (3): Crusader's Mantle, Revivify. 4th (3): Banishment, Death Ward. 5th (1): Holy Weapon. A Charisma caster of the ninth order, by the Measure's reckoning rather than any oath's.
The Knight makes three longsword attacks.
Plus 10 (3d6) radiant damage against fiends and undead.
When an ally within 30 feet drops to 0 hit points, the Knight may allow it to make a death saving throw immediately with advantage.

biography.value: Highlord of the Blue Dragonarmy. The best field commander on either side of the war, and Raistlin's half-sister, and she has not decided what that is worth to her.

description.value: Allies within 30 feet that can hear Kitiara add +2 to attack rolls against any creature she has marked as a target on her turn.
Kitiara has advantage on Insight checks made to determine an opponent's next move, and cannot be surprised while she has line of sight to the enemy.
Kitiara may reroll a failed saving throw.
Kitiara makes three longsword attacks.
Kitiara adds 4 to her AC against one melee attack that would hit her. She must see the attacker and be wielding a melee weapon.

biography.value: Head of the Red Robes, lame in the left leg from his own Test and cheerfully unembarrassed about it. The only Conclave member who treats Raistlin as a colleague, and therefore the most suspected man in the Tower.

description.value: When a creature within 30 feet casts a spell, Justarius may use his reaction to grant that spell advantage or impose disadvantage on its first attack roll or saving throw. He decides after seeing the target.

15th-level wizard. Spell save DC 18, +10 to hit. Cantrips: Cleaning, Borrowed Hue, Conjurer's Chalk, Mage Hand, Ray of Frost. 1st (4 slots): Shield, Mage Armor. 2nd (3): Misty Step, Mirror Image. 3rd (3): Counterspell, Dispel Magic. 4th (3): Fire Shield, Dimension Door, Polymorph. 5th (2): Telekinesis. 6th (1): Chain Lightning, Globe of Invulnerability. 7th (1): Reverse Gravity, Teleport. Order spells (Red Robes): Mirror Passage, Equal Exchange, Equilibrium Gate, Lunitari's Exchange, Wayreth's Moving Door, Mirror of Possible Selves.

Scribed and owned, and not among today's preparations; any of these can be prepared after a long rest. Spellbook (unprepared): Detect Magic, Comprehend Languages, Identify, Balanced Implement, Veil of the Ordinary, Stone Guardian, Arcane Staff, Lesser, Awaken the Mind, Phantom Architecture, Conjure Counterpart, Balanced Transformation, Mirror Labyrinth, Mindspin, Palace Between Moments.

biography.value: Senior Black Robe, and until Raistlin the most powerful on Ansalon. She is not plotting against him. She is waiting, which is worse.

description.value: Ladonna has advantage on Charisma checks made while telling the complete truth about her own motives, which is most of the time and disarms people far more effectively than lying.

16th-level wizard. Spell save DC 18, +10 to hit. Cantrips: Cinder Lash, Nuitari's Hook, Grave Whisper, Mage Hand, Minor Illusion. 1st (4 slots): Shield, Mage Armor. 2nd (3): Hold Person, Suggestion, Misty Step. 3rd (3): Fear, Counterspell, Dispel Magic. 4th (3): Greater Invisibility, Blight, Dimension Door. 5th (2): Dominate Person, Contact Other Plane. 7th (1): Finger of Death. 8th (1): Feeblemind. Order spells (Black Robes): Sable Edict, Tyrant's Brand, Curse the Magi, Death's Due, Edict of the Black Moon, Exsanguinate Memory.

Scribed and owned, and not among today's preparations; any of these can be prepared after a long rest. Spellbook (unprepared): Detect Magic, False Life, Borrowed Vitality, Obedient Step, Blackflame Dart, Blood Scent, Disarm, Feign Life, Harvest the Fallen, Black Moon Detonation, Life Transfer, Crown of Submission, Transfer Essence, Raistlin's Wheel of Flame, Soul Chain.

biography.value: Head of the Conclave. Former Master of Wayreth, declined by a building he had served for thirty years. He believes he did the right thing and cannot stop testing that belief.

description.value: Once per long rest Par-Salian may declare the Conclave's writ. Each Wizard of High Sorcery of his choice within 60 feet must succeed on a DC 19 Charisma saving throw or be unable to cast spells against him for 1 minute.

17th-level wizard. Spell save DC 19, +11 to hit. Cantrips: Guiding Sigil, Silver Ward, Steady Hand, Light, Mage Hand. 1st (4 slots): Shield, Mage Armor, Detect Magic. 2nd (3): Mirror Image, Misty Step. 3rd (3): Counterspell, Dispel Magic. 4th (3): Banishment, Dimension Door. 5th (2): Wall of Force, Scrying. 6th (1): True Seeing. 7th (1): Forcecage, Teleport. 8th (1): Antimagic Field. 9th (1): Foresight. Order spells (White Robes): Moonward, Oath of Clarity, Suppress Magic, Prism of Spellturning, Perfect Witness, Aegis of the Three Moons.

Scribed and owned, and not among today's preparations; any of these can be prepared after a long rest. Spellbook (unprepared): Identify, Protection from Evil and Good, Comprehend Languages, Detect Familiar, Kindled Resolve, Silver Reprieve, Truth-Testing, Concordant Courage, Spellward Relay, Unclouded Sight, Lantern of Unasked Truths, Sanctuary of Consent, Aegis of Solinari, Witness Chain, Greater Arcane Eye, Solinari's Interdiction.
Par-Salian spends the first three rounds of any combat attempting to end it. He is very good at ending them.

biography.value: Twenty-six years old and prematurely ruined. Golden skin, hourglass pupils, and a cough he manages with a draught he permits no one else to touch. This block exists so you know what happens if the party attacks him. They lose.

dr.custom: bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks

description.value: If Raistlin fails a saving throw, he can choose to succeed instead.

Raistlin sees all living things as they will be. He automatically knows the current hit points, conditions and remaining lifespan of any creature he can see, and cannot be surprised. He has disadvantage on Charisma (Persuasion) checks against living creatures — he cannot stop seeing them die.

At the start of each of his turns, roll a d20. On a 1, the cough takes him: he cannot take reactions and cannot cast spells with verbal components until the end of his next turn. He does not conceal this.
Raistlin does not suffer low sanction and gains high sanction benefits regardless of the black moon's phase. Nobody has established why.

Inside Wayreth, Raistlin knows the location of every creature in the building, cannot be surprised or teleported against his will, and any creature attacking him has disadvantage on its first attack roll each turn.

20th-level wizard. Spell save DC 22, +14 to hit. Cantrips: Cinder Lash, Grave Whisper, Nuitari's Hook, Mage Hand, Prestidigitation. 1st (4 slots): Shield, Mage Armor. 2nd (3): Mirror Image, Misty Step. 3rd (3): Counterspell, Dispel Magic. 4th (3): Banishment, Greater Invisibility. 5th (3): Wall of Force. 6th (2): Chain Lightning, Globe of Invulnerability, Disintegrate. 7th (2): Forcecage, Plane Shift, Teleport. 8th (1): Maze, Mind Blank. 9th (1): Time Stop. Order spells (Black Robes): Blackflame Dart, Borrowed Vitality, Curse the Magi, Raistlin's Wheel of Flame, Death's Due, Silence the Defiant, Soul Chain, Sable Cataclysm, Final Dominion. Reverse Death is in no spellbook of his. Whether it ever will be is the question the Tower is asking.

Scribed and owned, and not among today's preparations; any of these can be prepared after a long rest. Spellbook (unprepared): Alarm, Comprehend Languages, Detect Magic, Identify, Find Familiar, Magic Missile, Detect Thoughts, Invisibility, Suggestion, Blood Scent, Umbral Burst, Fireball, Fly, Sable Edict, Blight, Tyrant's Brand, Crown of Submission.
Raistlin stops time for 1d4 + 1 turns. He uses this to leave, not to win — he does not fight people he has already beaten.
Raistlin casts a cantrip.
Raistlin teleports up to 60 feet to a space he can see.

One creature Raistlin can see makes a DC 22 Wisdom saving throw, taking 18 (4d8) psychic damage and suffering disadvantage on its next attack roll on a failure, or half damage on a success. He does not appear to do anything.

biography.value: He has been writing the history of Krynn since before there was a Palanthas to write it in. He records. He does not direct, and he will explain the difference at length if you mistake the two.

languages.custom: every language that has ever been spoken

description.value: Astinus knows everything that has happened. Not what will happen — what has. He answers factual questions about the past truthfully and completely, and refuses every question about the future.
Astinus will not lift a hand to prevent anything, and cannot be persuaded, threatened, charmed or bargained into it. He has watched worse than this and written it down.

Astinus is immune to all damage and to every condition. He automatically succeeds on every saving throw. He cannot be moved, banished, restrained, polymorphed, imprisoned or planeshifted against his will, and magic that would read or alter his mind fails without a roll. Effects that would kill him outright, including power word kill and a failed death saving throw, have no effect.

Astinus's spellcasting ability is Intelligence (spell save DC 26). He casts the following spells at will, requiring no components. At will: comprehend languages, detect magic, detect thoughts, identify, zone of truth, legend lore, scrying, true seeing. Every one of them looks backward or looks now. He has no divination that touches the future, and refuses to be asked.

This block exists so you are not caught out, not so it can be used. Nothing the party can do to Astinus will work, and any attempt simply gets recorded — in his hand, in the volume for this year, while they are still trying.
He will not use it for this.

biography.value: The trees of Silvanesti bleed and scream. This one has been doing it for a year and has stopped being a tree in any useful sense.

description.value: A creature that hits the tree with a melee attack is sprayed with blood and must succeed on a DC 14 Wisdom saving throw or be frightened until the end of its next turn.
The tree cannot be moved from its space by any means short of destroying it. It does not need to see a target to attack it.
The tree makes two branch attacks.

biography.value: The trees around the Palanthas Tower. They do not pursue. They do not need to.

languages.custom: understands Common but does not speak

description.value: Any creature that starts its turn within 30 feet must succeed on a DC 16 Wisdom saving throw or be frightened until the start of its next turn. A frightened creature must spend its movement retreating if it can.
The sentinel does not attack any creature bearing the magical signature of the Tower's Master, and will bow its branches away from such a creature's path.

One creature grappled by the sentinel must succeed on a DC 16 Strength saving throw or be pulled beneath the soil, becoming restrained and unable to breathe. It takes 18 (4d8) necrotic damage at the start of each of its turns.

biography.value: Not zombies. Not skeletons. People — with names, families, training, and grief about what happened to them. Arc V.

description.value: The Returned has all the memories, skills and personality it had in life. It also obeys Raistlin Majere instinctively and immediately, and it knows that it does. Ask the player running one how that feels.
When the Returned drops to 0 hit points, it drops to 1 instead unless the damage was radiant or from a critical hit. Once per long rest.
The Returned makes two weapon attacks.

biography.value: They followed Soth into the fire and they have not been permitted to stop following him.

description.value: The knight cannot flee while its lord is on the field, and has advantage on saving throws against being turned while it can see him.
The knight makes two longsword attacks.

biography.value: The women who sang Soth's warning and were not heard. They are still singing.

description.value: The banshee can move through creatures and objects as difficult terrain, taking 5 (1d10) force damage if it ends its turn inside an object.
The banshee can magically sense the presence of living creatures up to 5 miles away and knows the general direction, though not their number or identity.

Each creature within 30 feet that can hear the banshee and is not undead must make a DC 14 Constitution saving throw. On a failure a creature drops to 0 hit points; on a success it takes 10 (3d6) psychic damage. 1/day.

biography.value: Level Ten of the Palanthas Tower. Fistandantilus restored these, and most of them obeyed him permanently, and they knew that they did. One will explain this calmly and ask not to be freed.

languages.custom: and four languages nobody has been able to identify

description.value: The experiment can converse, reason and negotiate. It knows precisely what was done to it and can describe the ritual in technical detail, which is the most valuable thing in the room.
If a creature speaks Fistandantilus's true binding phrase, the experiment must obey it for 1 hour and cannot warn anyone that this has happened.
The experiment makes two withering touch attacks.

One creature within 30 feet must make a DC 16 Constitution saving throw, taking 36 (8d8) necrotic damage on a failure and having its hit point maximum reduced by the same amount until it finishes a long rest. Recharge 5-6.

biography.value: Arc V. He is alive, warm, and himself. And when his brother gives him an instruction he obeys it faster than a brother should.

description.value: Caramon obeys any direct instruction from Raistlin Majere immediately and without hesitation. He is aware that he does. He has not told his brother how much this frightens him.
Caramon dreams of somewhere beyond the world. He will tell the party, privately, that he does not know whether he came back because he wanted to.
Caramon may reroll a failed saving throw once per long rest.
Caramon makes three greatsword attacks.
When a creature Caramon can see attacks a target within 5 feet of him, he may make himself the target instead.

biography.value: Wizards of High Sorcery who petitioned to remain. They volunteered, they remember being people, and they will explain the rules before they act.

description.value: The Guardian cannot leave its Tower and cannot be permanently destroyed within it. Reduced to 0 hit points, it reforms at the door it was set to guard after 24 hours. It is fully aware of this, and it makes them very calm.

The Guardian attacks only creatures violating the Tower's rules of conduct, and stops the instant the violation stops. It will accept a surrender. It explains the rules first, in a voice that is politely apologetic.
The Guardian makes two chill touch attacks.

One creature within 30 feet must make a DC 17 Wisdom saving throw. On a failure it is frightened for 1 minute and sees, clearly, the moment of its own death. It may repeat the save at the end of each of its turns. Recharge 5-6.

biography.value: Two hundred years dead and entirely undeterred by it. He does not want to possess Raistlin. He expects Raistlin to finish the work voluntarily, and he has excellent evidence.

dr.custom: bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks

description.value: If Fistandantilus fails a saving throw, he can choose to succeed instead.
Fistandantilus can restore a creature that has died within the last century as an action, provided he holds an anchor to it. The restored creature obeys him, knows that it obeys him, and cannot stop.
Fistandantilus opens every encounter by explaining precisely what he wants and what he will give for it. Everything he offers, he delivers.

20th-level wizard. Spell save DC 22, +14 to hit. Cantrips: Chill Touch, Grave Whisper, Nuitari's Hook, Mage Hand, Minor Illusion. 1st (4 slots): Shield, Mage Armor. 2nd (3): Mirror Image, Misty Step. 3rd (3): Counterspell, Dispel Magic, Animate Dead. 4th (3): Blight, Dimension Door. 5th (3): Dominate Person. 6th (2): Contingency, Create Undead, Globe of Invulnerability. 7th (2): Forcecage, Finger of Death. 8th (1): Power Word Stun. 9th (1): Time Stop, Wish. Order spells (Black Robes): Feign Life, Harvest the Fallen, Life Transfer, Transfer Essence, Curse the Magi, Death's Due, Soul Chain, Exsanguinate Memory, Reverse Death.

Scribed and owned, and not among today's preparations; any of these can be prepared after a long rest. Spellbook (unprepared): Identify, Detect Magic, Comprehend Languages, Alarm, Find Familiar, False Life, Blood Scent, Disarm, Umbral Burst, Suggestion, Hold Person, Fireball, Sable Edict, Bestow Curse, Contact Other Plane, Magic Jar, Clone.
The target's hit point maximum is reduced by the damage taken until it finishes a long rest.

One creature within 60 feet must succeed on a DC 22 Charisma saving throw or be charmed for 1 minute. While charmed it must obey Fistandantilus's commands. It repeats the save if it takes damage or is ordered to harm someone it loves.
Fistandantilus casts a cantrip.
Fistandantilus makes one Withering Touch attack and regains hit points equal to the damage dealt.

Fistandantilus alters one thing that happened in the last round — an attack that hit now missed, a save that succeeded now failed. He may do this once per encounter regardless of remaining legendary actions.

actors.name: Lord Soth, Knight of the Black Rose

biography.value: Damned for a failure of courage he had every opportunity to correct. He does not serve Takhisis so much as tolerate her, and he recognises what Raistlin is becoming faster than anyone alive.

dr.custom: bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks that aren't silvered

description.value: If Soth fails a saving throw, he can choose to succeed instead.
Soth is immune to effects that turn undead.

Any creature that starts its turn within 30 feet must succeed on a DC 19 Wisdom saving throw or be frightened for 1 minute. A frightened creature repeats the save at the end of each of its turns. On a success it is immune for 24 hours.
Soth cannot be deceived about his own history and has advantage on Insight checks against any creature attempting to justify a choice it regrets. He will say so, and it is worse than an attack.
Soth makes three longsword attacks, or two and uses Hellfire Orb or Banshee Wail.
Plus 13 (3d8) fire damage.

Soth hurls a magical ball of fire at a point within 120 feet. Each creature in a 20-foot radius makes a DC 20 Dexterity saving throw, taking 35 (10d6) fire and 35 (10d6) necrotic damage on a failure, or half on a success.
Soth's attendant banshees wail. Each creature within 30 feet that can hear must make a DC 19 Constitution saving throw or drop to 0 hit points. On a success it takes 10 (3d6) psychic damage.
Soth makes one longsword attack.
Soth targets one frightened creature within 60 feet. It must succeed on a DC 19 Wisdom saving throw or use its reaction to move up to its speed away from Soth by the safest route.
Soth moves up to his speed and makes one longsword attack with advantage.

prototypeToken.name: Lord Soth, Knight of the Black Rose
